extracted.intended_audience: aircraft operators, maintenance personnel, repair stations, and FAA certification/inspection staff
extracted.subtask_description: Federal Aviation Administration final rules (airworthiness directives) establishing mandatory inspection, repair, replacement, reporting, and compliance procedures for specific aircraft/parts to address safety issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal and replacement of Bell 204B tail rotor gearbox duplex bearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Within the next 100 hours’ time in service after the effective date of this AD, remove the tail rotor gearbox duplex bearing set, P/N 204-040-424-001, from service and replace with a serviceable part before further flight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance is required as indicated, unless already accomplished. Purpose: to prevent failure of the tail rotor duplex bearing which could result in loss of tail rotor control and subsequent loss of the helicopter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ferry flight permission for Bell 204B to accomplish AD
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with FAR §§ 21.197 and 21.199, the helicopter may be flown to a base where the requirements of this AD may be accomplished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows a ferry/special flight to a location where replacement/repairs can be done; normal restrictions of FAR 21.197/21.199 apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate method of compliance (AMOC) approval for Bell 204B
rubrics_metrics.description: An alternate method of compliance or adjustment of the compliance time which provides an equivalent level of safety may be used when approved by the Manager, Rotorcraft Certification Office, ASW-170, Rotorcraft Directorate, FAA, Southwest Region, Fort Worth, Texas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for AMOCs should be sent to the named manager; approval is required before using an alternate means or different compliance timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspection threshold for Boeing 767 8th stage bleed check valve (initial)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within the next 250 hours time-in-service after the effective date of this AD, or prior to accumulating 600 hours total time-in-service on the valve, whichever occurs later, perform the inspections of the check valve in accordance with Boeing Alert Service Bulletin 767-36A0030, dated April 27, 1989.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize inspection timing per the threshold; carry out inspections exactly as Boeing Alert Service Bulletin 767-36A0030. Purpose: prevent engine shutdown or damage and/or pneumatic system damage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repair/replace failing Boeing 767 check valves before further flight
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to further flight, repair or replace check valves which do not pass all required inspections called out in Boeing Alert Service Bulletin 767-36A0030.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any valve failing inspection must not remain in service; ensure repairs meet procedures in the service bulletin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspection/repair requirement for used check valves before installation (Boeing 767)
rubrics_metrics.description: Used check valves must be inspected and repaired, if necessary, in accordance with Boeing Alert Service Bulletin 767-36A0030 dated April 27, 1989, prior to installation in any Model 767 series airplane.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-installation inspection/repair of used parts prevents introducing defective components into the fleet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminating action by installing P/N 320544-1 valve (Boeing 767)
rubrics_metrics.description: Installation of a P/N 320544-1 valve in lieu of a P/N 3202164-2 or -4 valve constitutes terminating action for the inspection required by this AD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replacement with the redesigned valve eliminates the need for the repetitive inspections mandated by the AD.

rubrics_metrics.name: AMOC approval and routing for Boeing 767 check valve AD
rubrics_metrics.description: An alternate means of compliance or adjustment of the compliance time, which provides an acceptable level of safety, may be used when approved by the Manager, Seattle Aircraft Certification Office, FAA, Northwest Mountain Region. Note: The request should be forwarded through an FAA Principal Maintenance Inspector (PMI), who will either concur or comment and then send it to the Manager, Seattle Aircraft Certification Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the PMI forwarding procedure when requesting AMOC; approval authority is the Seattle Aircraft Certification Office Manager.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special flight permits for Boeing 767 check valve AD
rubrics_metrics.description: Special flight permits may be issued in accordance with FAR 21.197 and 21.199 to operate airplanes to a base for the accomplishment of the inspections required by this AD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operators may ferry aircraft to a maintenance location under the provisions of FAR 21.197/21.199 to perform required AD work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repetitive inspection schedule for Belianca drag strut landing gear fitting assemblies
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon the accumulation of 500 hours total time-in-service (TIS), or within the next 100 hours TIS after the effective date of this AD, whichever occurs later, and each 100 hours TIS thereafter, inspect the left and right drag strut landing gear fitting assemblies, Part Number (P/N) 194153-10, for cracks, deformations, or failures as specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes the initial and repetitive inspection intervals to detect cracks/deformations that could lead to landing gear collapse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed inspection procedure for Belianca P/N 194153-10 fittings
rubrics_metrics.description: (a)(1)-(3) Place jacks or other workstands under the airplane at locations specified in the Belianca Service Manual; (2) clean the aft face of the -1 fitting with Stoddart solvent and a brush; (3) inspect for cracks adjacent to the welds joining the -1 fitting to the -2 fitting and -3 brace near the lower aft attachment bolt holes using liquid penetrant inspection techniques and a magnifying glass.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note 1: Penetrant inspection techniques are described in FAA Advisory Circular (AC) 43-3 'Nondestructive Testing in Aircraft.' These inspections can be conducted with the fitting assemblies installed on the airplane. Do not apply loads to the landing gear components during inspection as it may move the drag strut to overcenter and cause collapse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement requirement for cracked Belianca fittings
rubrics_metrics.description: If any crack is found (during the penetrant inspection), prior to further flight replace the assembly with a new fitting assembly, P/N 194153-30 or P/N 194153-40, as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any detected cracks mandate immediate replacement before further flight to prevent gear collapse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance criterion and replacement for local deformation of Belianca fitting
rubrics_metrics.description: Lay a straight-edge alongside the lower aft attachment bolts and, using a feeler gage or wire gage of .030 inch thickness, look for any evidence of local deformation (dimpling) in the -1 fitting. If any deformation greater than .030 inches is found, prior to further flight replace the assembly with a new fitting assembly, P/N 194153-30 or P/N 194153-40, as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the deformation tolerance (.030 inch) beyond which replacement is mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drag strut overcenter check and adjustment (Belianca)
rubrics_metrics.description: Check and adjust, as required, the drag strut for correct overcenter using the appropriate procedures in the Belianca Service Manual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper overcenter prevents gear unlocking; adjustment instructions are in the manufacturer's manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection and repeat inspection when no defects found (Belianca)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the inspections specified do not indicate any evidence of cracks or local deformation in the -1 fitting, apply zinc chromate or Epibond primer, as necessary, to protect the part and repeat these inspections as specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrosion/paint protection plus continued periodic inspections are required to maintain safety margin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption from repetitive inspections for P/N 194153-30 and -40 (Belianca)
rubrics_metrics.description: The repetitive inspections specified are not required on the P/N 194153-30 or P/N 194153-40 assemblies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thicker replacement assemblies (-30/-40) are considered not susceptible in the same way and thus exempt from the repetitive inspection requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditional special flight permit for Belianca cracked/deformed fittings
rubrics_metrics.description: Airplanes with cracked or deformed fittings may be flown with a special flight permit in accordance with FAR 21.197 to a location where this AD may be accomplished provided that no crack is found during the inspection of paragraph (a)(3) that exceeds % in. length, or no deformation is found during the inspection of paragraph (a)(4) that is great enough to cause the overcenter of the drag strut to be out of tolerance. In these cases, no special flight permit is allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text includes a size threshold (garbled here as '% in.') and prohibits special flight permits when cracks/deformations exceed those thresholds; operators must follow FAR 21.197 limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: AMOC approval and routing for Belianca AD
rubrics_metrics.description: An alternate method of compliance or adjustment of the initial and repetitive compliance times, which provides an equivalent level of safety, may be approved by the Manager, Chicago Aircraft Certification Office, 2300 E. Devon Avenue, Des Plaines, Illinois 60018. Note: The request should be forwarded through an FAA Maintenance Inspector, who may add comments and send it to the Manager, Chicago Aircraft Certification Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for alternatives go through the local FAA maintenance inspector to the named Manager for approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: HFEC inspection threshold and repeat interval for Boeing 747 lower-lobe lap joints
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct a high frequency eddy current (HFEC) inspection of the lower lobe lap joints in the vicinity of the wing-to-body fairing to detect cracks, in accordance with Boeing Alert Service Bulletin 747-53A2312 dated June 12, 1989, at the following thresholds: (1) For airplanes <11,200 landings: prior to accumulation of 11,000 landings or within next 1,000 landings after effective date, whichever later; (2) For 11,200–15,200 landings: within next 1,000 landings or prior to 15,500 landings, whichever first; (3) For 15,201–18,200 landings: within next 300 landings or prior to 18,250 landings; (4) For >18,200 landings: within next 50 landings. Repeat this inspection at intervals not to exceed 4,000 landings until the airplane is modified as described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thresholds depend on accumulated landings; use Boeing Alert Service Bulletin procedures for HFEC inspection; repeated inspections required until modification (terminating action) is done.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repair requirement for cracks in Boeing 747 lap joints
rubrics_metrics.description: Repair any cracks detected, prior to further flight, in accordance with Boeing Alert Service Bulletin 747-53A2312 dated June 12, 1989.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detected cracking must be repaired immediately per the manufacturer's repair instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written reporting requirement after initial Boeing 747 inspection
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 10 days after the completion of the initial inspection required by paragraph A, submit a written report of the location and quantity of all affected countersunk fasteners found, along with aircraft line number and the number of flight cycles, to the Manager, Seattle Aircraft Certification Office, FAA, Northwest Mountain Region.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely reporting of findings supports FAA monitoring of the issue and fleet-wide response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modification as terminating action for Boeing 747 lap joint inspections
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to the accumulation of 20,000 landings or within the next 3,000 landings after the effective date of the AD, whichever occurs later, modify the airplane by replacing countersunk fasteners in the upper row of the lower lobe lap joints in the vicinity of the wing-to-body fairing with protruding head fasteners, in accordance with Boeing Alert Service Bulletin 747-53A2312, dated June 12, 1989. This modification constitutes terminating action for the inspections required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modification replaces susceptible fasteners with protruding-head fasteners and ends the inspection requirement once accomplished.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of terminating condition for Boeing 747
rubrics_metrics.description: Verification that an affected airplane does not have countersunk fasteners in the upper row of the lower lobe lap joints in the vicinity of the wing-to-body fairing as described in Boeing Alert Service Bulletin 747-53A2312 constitutes terminating action from the requirements of this AD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A configuration check showing the required fasteners are already installed negates inspection requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of landings for compliance timing (Boeing 747)
rubrics_metrics.description: For the purpose of complying with the AD, the number of landings may be determined to equal the number of pressurization cycles where the cabin pressure differential was greater than 2.0 psi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that pressurization cycles over 2.0 psi count as 'landings' for compliance timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjustment factor for Model 747SR compliance times
rubrics_metrics.description: For Model 747SR airplanes only, based on continued mixed operation of lower cabin differentials, the inspection and modification compliance times specified in this AD may be multiplied by a 1.2 adjustment factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives a scaling factor for SR variant operating characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: AMOC approval and PMI routing for Boeing 747 AD
rubrics_metrics.description: An alternate means of compliance or adjustment of the compliance time, which provides an acceptable level of safety, may be used when approved by the Manager, Seattle Aircraft Certification Office, FAA, Northwest Mountain Region. Note: The request should be forwarded through an FAA Principal Maintenance Inspector (PMI), who will either concur or comment, and then send it to the Manager, Seattle Aircraft Certification Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow PMI forwarding process for AMOC requests; Seattle ACO Manager is approval authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special flight permits for Boeing 747 AD
rubrics_metrics.description: Special flight permits may be issued in accordance with FAR 21.197 and 21.199 to operate airplanes to a base in order to comply with the requirements of this AD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operators may use special flight permits under FAR to reach a maintenance base to perform required inspections or modifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rework/inspection requirement for Boeing 767 entry/service door acoustical seal
rubrics_metrics.description: This AD requires rework, or inspection and rework, of the acoustical seal for entry/service doors to ensure proper arming of the emergency evacuation slide, in accordance with Boeing Service Bulletin 767-25-0123. Revision 1, dated September 14, 1989, is approved and compliance may be made in accordance with this revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures the acoustical seal does not migrate and interfere with girt bar carrier rotation, which could result in incomplete arming of the slide. Operators may use the Revision 1 of the service bulletin as an optional means of compliance.
